title: Marginal rate of technical substitution (MRTS)
plain:
Moving along an isoquant means giving up some of one input and making up for it with the other. The **marginal rate of technical substitution** says at what rate: how many units of capital one more unit of labor can replace while output stays the same.
$$MRTS_{KL} = \frac{MP_L}{MP_K}$$
It is the **absolute value of the slope** of the isoquant (Reading Quiz Q2: both the substitution rate and the absolute slope). The slides write it as \(MP_L / MP_K = \partial K / \partial L \approx \Delta K / \Delta L\).

Why the ratio of marginal products: one more worker adds \(MP_L\) units. To keep output fixed you must drop that many units' worth of capital, which is \(MP_L / MP_K\) units of K.

By production function:
- Linear: \(MRTS = b/a\), constant.
- Cobb-Douglas: \(MRTS = \frac{bK}{aL}\), changes along the isoquant.
- Leontief: undefined.

Example: \(Q = K^{0.5}L^{0.5}\) at K = 20, L = 5 gives \(MRTS = K/L = 4\): one more worker can replace 4 units of capital.
why: The MRTS is the slope that cost minimization compares with the input price ratio w/r (S16-05).
definition: The MRTS is the rate at which a producer can substitute between two inputs and maintain the same level of output. It equals MP_L / MP_K, the absolute value of the slope of the isoquant.

formulas.name: Cobb-Douglas MRTS
formulas.note: The ratio MP_L/MP_K is on the sheet; the simplified bK/(aL) you derive with exponent rules.

derivation: Along an isoquant output does not change: \(MP_L\,\Delta L + MP_K\,\Delta K = 0\). Rearranged: \(-\frac{\Delta K}{\Delta L} = \frac{MP_L}{MP_K}\). The left side is the absolute slope of the isoquant.

math.title: Exponent rules (S15 slides pp. 36 to 42)
math.body:
- Multiply, same base: add exponents. \(a^x a^y = a^{x+y}\)
- Divide, same base: subtract. \(\frac{a^x}{a^y} = a^{x-y}\)
- Power of a product: \((xy)^a = x^a y^a\)
- Power of a quotient: \(\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)^a = \frac{x^a}{y^a}\)
- Power of a power: multiply. \((a^x)^y = a^{xy}\)
- Zero power: \(x^0 = 1\)
- Negative power is a reciprocal: \(x^{-a} = \frac{1}{x^a}\), so \(L^{-0.5} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L}}\)
- Fractional power is a root: \(x^{0.5} = \sqrt{x}\), \(x^{0.25} = \sqrt[4]{x}\)

On a calculator: \(16^{0.25}\) is 16, then the \(y^x\) or ^ key, then 0.25. Answer 2.

worked.title: Cobb-Douglas MRTS
worked.answer: MRTS = 9: one more unit of labor replaces 9 units of capital at this point.

graph.caption: The dashed line is tangent to the isoquant; its slope (absolute value) is the MRTS. Slide the point to see the MRTS change.

traps: MRTS is MP_L / MP_K, not MP_K / MP_L. Labor on top.
MRTS is about substituting INPUTS while holding OUTPUT constant, not substituting outputs (Reading Quiz Q2 distractor).
The slope of the isoquant is negative; the MRTS is its absolute value.
For linear production the MRTS does not depend on K and L.
In bK/(aL) keep a with K and b with L: b (labor's exponent) goes on top with K.
